title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 382
paragraphs: Whether the Greeks have learned this also from the Egyptians, I cannot say for certain, since I see that the Thracians too, and the Scythians, Persians, Lydians, and almost all the barbarians regard those of their citizens who learn the crafts, and their descendants, as less honorable than the rest; while those who keep themselves free from all practice of manual arts are reckoned noble, and especially those devoted to war. However that may be, the Greeks have all learned this, and especially the Lacedemonians; but the Corinthians least of all look down on those who practice handicrafts.
